rows.name: player_x_position (Mario horizontal position in the level)
rows.notes: Encoding: one byte, the level x-coordinate modulo 256; it is the coordinate the engine scrolls the level in, so it wraps at 256 as the 256-pixel screen scrolls (observed 251 -> 9 during a run). Mario's on-screen x is derived in ROM routine at CPU $F171: LDA $0086 (indexed), SEC, SBC $071C (scroll), STA $03AD. Proof (differential + write): snapshot_memory/play_input/diff_memory narrowed holding Right from 167 to 41 survivors, $0005/$03AD/$0755/$0086 all tracking screen x; the writer of $03AD was disassembled to $0086 - $071C; then write_memory $0086 = 200 (0xC8) while paused and stepping frames moved Mario from screen x=40 to x=200 (screenshot: Mario standing at the right-hand bush instead of the start hill). Writing the derived copies $03AD/$0755 alone had no effect (snapped back), so $0086 is the master. No separate player page byte was found: the level page is tracked only by the scroll $071C and the nametable. Source: differential search.

rows.name: player_y_position (Mario vertical position)
rows.notes: Encoding: one byte, the screen y of the top of Mario's sprite box; on the ground in 1-1 it reads 176, and it decreases as Mario rises (jump) and increases as he falls. Proof (differential + write): diff s3->s4 with filter 'decreased' after holding A for 10 frames showed $00CE 176 -> 141 (a copy moves with it at $03B8, 176 -> 141, and Mario's OAM y entries $0204/$0208 176 -> 141); then write_memory $00CE = 120 (0x78) while paused and stepping 2 frames left Mario hanging in mid-air at y~120 (screenshot: Mario floating in the sky above the bushes instead of standing on the ground). Source: differential search.

rows.name: world_number
rows.notes: Encoding: the current world number, 0 = World 1, so World 1-1 holds 0. Proof (write + screenshot of the death card): in World 1-1, $075F read 0; write_memory $075F = 4 (together with $075C = 2), then held Right ~300 frames to die and let the card draw; the resulting screenshot showed both the fixed HUD and the black card reading 'WORLD 5-3' (world digit 5 = 4+1, level digit 3 = 2+1). The two values were distinct in the two positions, which fixes which address is world and which is level. Source: differential search / own judgement for a value that does not change by playing.

rows.name: level_number
rows.notes: Encoding: the level number within the current world, 0 = the first level of the world, so World 1-1 holds 0. Proof (write + screenshot of the death card): $075C read 0 in 1-1; write_memory $075C = 2 (with $075F = 4), died by holding Right, and the 'WORLD 5-3' card screenshot confirmed the second digit is this byte (2 -> 3). Kept as the level number, not the world, because the two test values appeared in the positions matching their addresses. Source: differential search / own judgement for a value that does not change by playing.

rows.name: screen_scroll_x (level's left edge, mod 256)
rows.notes: Supporting variable found while chasing the horizontal position. $03AD (Mario's on-screen x) is computed as $0086 - $071C in the ROM routine at CPU $F171, so $071C is the x of the level's left edge (scroll) modulo 256. Watched during a hold-Right run: it climbed 1,6,14,24,38,...,119 and froze at 119 while Mario was blocked at a pipe at $0086=63 (screen x = 63-119 = 200). It does not wrap with Mario's byte (the two are on different 256-pixel pages once Mario has crossed one). Source: differential search.

rows.name: player_screen_x (derived on-screen x of Mario)
rows.notes: Derived copy: ROM routine at CPU $F171 does LDA $0086,X / SEC / SBC $071C / STA $03AD,Y, so $03AD = player_x ($0086) - scroll ($071C) = Mario's x on the visible screen. Written every frame (trace_writes on $03AD gave PC $F17F, prgRom 0x717F, 60 writes in 30 frames). Writing $03AD directly has no effect: after write_memory $03AD = 200 and stepping one frame it was back to 40. Do not use it to move Mario; write $0086 instead. Source: differential search plus disassembly.
